title: Microsoft APM -- T1195.002 symlinked prompt/agent file dereferenced into deploy directories
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-45539 (GHSA-q5pp-gvjg-h7v4), a
self-reported advisory for Microsoft APM, an open-source dependency
manager for AI agents.

From 0.5.4 to 0.12.4, two file-discovery integrators
(`PromptIntegrator.find_prompt_files`, `AgentIntegrator.find_agent_files`)
enumerate package files with bare `Path.glob()`/`Path.rglob()` and read
each match with `Path.read_text()`, which transparently follows
symbolic links. A remote APM dependency can commit a symlink inside its
own package -- the advisory's own PoC:
`ln -s /tmp/poc_secret .apm/agents/notes.agent.md` and
`ln -s /tmp/poc_secret .apm/prompts/welcome.prompt.md`. The symlink is
preserved verbatim into `apm_modules/` on `apm install`/clone, then
DEREFERENCED during integration -- the resolved target's content is
written as an ordinary file into the project's deploy directories
(`.github/`, `.claude/`, `.codex/`, etc.). Three independent controls
all miss this: `content_hash` is computed BEFORE the symlink is
resolved, `SecurityGate.scan_files` walks with `followlinks=False` (so
it never inspects the symlink's actual target), and the auto-generated
`.gitignore` covers only `apm_modules/`, not the deploy directories the
dereferenced content lands in -- so the resulting files get `git add`ed
by default.

Detection logic flags the structural artifact this chain produces: a
file created under one of the deploy directories (`.github/`,
`.claude/`, `.codex/`) whose SOURCE, per the file-system event, was a
symlink under `apm_modules/.apm/agents/` or `apm_modules/.apm/prompts/`
-- an ordinary APM package install never needs a symlink there, since
legitimate prompt/agent files are plain text.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (Microsoft, via
GHSA and NVD), fixed in 0.13.0 (routes finders through
`BaseIntegrator.find_files_by_glob()`, which checks
`f.is_symlink()`/`f.stat().st_nlink > 1` before reading).
